# pqtools

> Run, lint and format Power Query M without Power BI. pqtools executes a `.pq`
> query end to end against local CSV files in pure Python (no dependencies), and
> is also a linter, formatter and safe renamer for M source - including the
> queries stored inside `.pbix`, `.pbit` and `.xlsx` files.

Install with `pip install pqtools`. Python 3.11+. MIT. Unofficial; not
affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft.

## What it does

- `pq eval report.pq` - run a query. Local-file sources (`Csv.Document`,
  `File.Contents`, `Text.FromBinary`) run natively, then the whole
  transformation chain: `Table.PromoteHeaders`, `Table.TransformColumnTypes`,
  `Table.SelectRows`, `Table.Group`, all six `JoinKind` values, pivot/unpivot,
  `List.*`, `Text.*`, `Number.*`, and date/time/duration. 640 M builtins.
  Output as JSON or CSV.
- The M operators follow the specification's own operand tables, not just the
  numeric rows: `null` propagates through arithmetic instead of raising,
  `#date + #duration` and `#datetime - #datetime` work, `8 / 0` is
  `#infinity`, binaries and logicals order, and `&` merges records, joins a
  date with a time, and concatenates lists as well as text.
- `pq list report.pbix` - name every query inside a .pbix / .pbit / .xlsx.
  Each name is usable directly as `pq eval FILE --member NAME`.
- `pq eval report.pbix --member Sales` - run one query out of a container,
  including the inline "Enter Data" tables Power BI embeds as a base64
  deflate payload.
- `pq check report.pq` - lint, with CI-shaped exit codes.
- `pq format report.pq` - format, via Microsoft's own pinned
  `@microsoft/powerquery-formatter`.
- `pq rename report.pq --from Old --to New` - rename a `let` binding without a
  find-and-replace hitting a matching string literal.
- Reads `.pbix` / `.pbit` / `.xlsx` containers to analyse the M inside them.
  `pq format` / `pq rename` / `pq replace-source` print the edited M and
  save it with `--write`. `pq add --name N --source '...' --write` adds a
  brand-new query. Any `--write` on a container writes a backup first, to the
  first free `<file>.bak`, `<file>.bak.1`, ... - an existing backup is never
  overwritten, and a backup that fails stops the edit.

<!-- coverage:start -->
pqtools registers **547 of the 635 names** in Microsoft's Power Query M reference - 86% of NAMES, which is not a measure of semantic compatibility and should not be quoted as one. Each registered name's arity and nullability are checked against its own reference page, and 141 of Microsoft's worked examples reproduce their documented output exactly; see SUPPORT-MATRIX.md for what is and is not measured. Every one of the remaining 88 is recognised by name and refuses with a typed error saying which outside system it would need - never a wrong answer, and never the bare "unknown identifier" that a typo produces.
<!-- coverage:end -->

## What it deliberately does NOT do

This matters more than the feature list, because guessing here produces a wrong
answer that looks right.

- It does not fold queries. Power Query rewrites `Table.SelectRows` into a
  `WHERE` clause and makes the remote engine do the work; pqtools fetches and
  filters locally. Results agree; the work happens in a different place, and
  on a large remote table that difference is the whole performance story.
  pandas does not fold either.
- It does not run `SharePoint.*`, which needs a tenant identity there is no
  honest way to stand in for. It raises a typed `M_EVAL_UNSUPPORTED` naming
  itself. `Table.Fuzzy*` is refused the same way: the similarity algorithm is
  not documented precisely enough to reproduce, and an approximate join
  returns wrong rows rather than an error.
- Connectors that ARE implemented - `Web.Contents`, `OData.Feed`,
  `Folder.Files`, `Folder.Contents`, `Excel.Workbook`, `Sql.Database`,
  `PostgreSQL.Database`, `MySQL.Database`, `Oracle.Database`, `Odbc.Query`,
  `Odbc.DataSource` - are OFF BY DEFAULT and refuse with `M_IO_BLOCKED`
  naming the flag that would enable them (`--allow-net`, `--allow-db`). The
  query names the destination, and the query is often somebody else's file.
  Even under `--allow-net`, internal and link-local addresses stay blocked
  (169.254.169.254 is the cloud metadata endpoint) unless
  `--allow-private-net` is also passed.
- It is not a Power Query replacement and does not reimplement the Mashup
  Engine.
- It never approximates. Any construct it cannot evaluate exactly raises a
  typed error naming it, rather than returning a plausible wrong value.
- It carries Microsoft's ENTIRE documented function list (`pqtools.catalog`,
  generated from Microsoft Learn by `scripts/sync_m_catalog.py`). A documented
  function it does not implement refuses with a message saying which outside
  system it would need; a name that is not M at all still reports "unknown
  identifier". Those are different problems with different fixes, so do not
  describe an unimplemented function as "not a Power Query function".
- It does NOT register any name Power Query lacks. `tests/test_catalog.py`
  enforces this against Microsoft's reference, because a function that exists
  here and not in Power Query means a query passes here and fails there -
  worse than a missing function. Two such names shipped by mistake before
  0.10.0 (`Uri.UnescapeDataString`, `Table.SelectDuplicates`) and are removed;
  neither should be reintroduced or recommended.
- Excel itself has never opened a workbook this rewrote (Excel was not
  installed where the write path was validated). The rebuild is verified four
  ways - CRC intact, every member except the DataMashup part byte-identical,
  the M reading back, and openpyxl opening the result to the same sheets and
  values - and every `--write` leaves a backup sidecar. Do not describe writing as
  unsafe, and do not describe it as Excel-certified.
- It sends no telemetry, and makes no network call unless the query asks
  for one AND the caller passed `--allow-net` or `--allow-db`.

## Correct usage

Run a query whose source is a local CSV - nothing to supply:

```bash
pq eval report.pq --format csv
```

Run a query whose source needs an engine, or whose path belongs to the machine
that authored it - bind the source step instead:

```bash
pq eval report.pq --bind Source=data.csv
```

From Python (this is the import that works; `evaluate` is exported at the
package root):

```python
from pqtools import evaluate

rows = evaluate(query_text, bindings={"Source": [{"a": 1}]})
```

A table is `list[dict[str, Any]]`. `Csv.Document` does NOT promote headers -
it returns `Column1..ColumnN`, and `Table.PromoteHeaders` is a separate step,
exactly as in Power Query.

## Error codes and exit status

Every failure is a typed error - never a traceback, never a plausible wrong
value. On the command line it prints as `error CODE: message` on stderr; with
`--json` it is one object on stderr, `{"code": "...", "message": "..."}`.
Exit status is 0 on success and 2 on any error, and 2 from `pq check` when a
diagnostic of severity `error` exists (warnings alone exit 0). From Python the
same classes are raised, each carrying the code as `.code`.

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `M_PARSE_ERROR` | The source is not valid M. It comes from Microsoft's own parser, so Power Query rejects it too. | Fix the query. |
| `M_EVAL_ERROR` | The query parsed and a step failed: wrong arity, wrong type, a missing column, an argument a builtin refuses. The message names the function. | Fix the query, not the tool. |
| `M_EVAL_UNSUPPORTED` | A deliberate refusal. The construct needs an outside system (a SharePoint tenant, the Mashup Engine, a credential store) or is not reproduced on purpose (`Table.Fuzzy*`, `Username`/`Password` inside an M record). The message names what it would need. | Do not retry, and do not approximate around it. Report it as unsupported here, not as broken M. |
| `M_IO_BLOCKED` | Policy, not failure. The query names a network or database source and the caller did not pass `--allow-net` / `--allow-db`, or the address is private or link-local and `--allow-private-net` was not passed. | Pass a flag only when the human you work for intends that destination. The query names it; the caller does not. |
| `M_IO_ERROR` | The operating system refused a read or write: a missing file, permissions, a directory where a file was expected. | Check the path. |
| `M_CONTAINER_ERROR` | A `.pbix` / `.pbit` / `.xlsx` could not be read, or a rebuilt one failed its own verification. Nothing was written. | Report it; do not retry with `--write`. |
| `M_SAFE_WRITE_REFUSED` | A `--write` was refused: the file changed under the lock, the lock could not be taken, the input exceeds 10 MiB, or it is not valid UTF-8. Nothing was written. | Re-run once the file is stable. Never work around it by writing the file yourself. |
| `M_RENAME_REFUSED` | `pq rename` could not prove the rename safe: a reserved keyword, a collision with an existing binding, a target that already appears in the source, overlapping spans. Nothing was written. | Choose another name or edit by hand. Scope: SUPPORT-MATRIX.md, "Refactoring scope". |
| `M_ADAPTER_ERROR` | An external adapter failed. Either the Fabric transport returned something malformed, empty, timed out, or over its 10 MiB limit; or the PQTest adapter refused its configuration (not Windows, not a user-installed `.exe`, wrong version), exited non-zero, timed out, or its output could not be read in full. | Read the message - it names the adapter. Fabric messages are remote: report them, nothing local is wrong. PQTest messages beginning with a configuration refusal are local: fix the path or the version. |
| `NODE_ERROR` | Node.js 22 or newer was not found or was refused (it will not run a `node` found in the current directory); or the bridge process itself failed: it timed out (30 s), its output exceeded 10 MiB, its output could not be read in full, or its input could not be written in full - the last two are a local pipe fault, not a Node fault. Every command that parses M spawns Node to reach Microsoft's parser. | Install Node 22+, or point `MQUERY_NODE` at it. A message naming a timeout or a pipe fault means nothing about the query is wrong: retry once. |
| `MQUERY_ERROR` | The base code: any other typed failure. | Read the message. |

## Credentials

Database credentials come from the environment and only from the environment:
`PQTOOLS_SQL_USER` / `PQTOOLS_SQL_PASSWORD` for `Sql.Database`, `PQTOOLS_PG_*`
for `PostgreSQL.Database`, `PQTOOLS_MYSQL_*` for `MySQL.Database`,
`PQTOOLS_ORACLE_*` for `Oracle.Database`. A `Username` or `Password` field in
the M options record is refused by name with `M_EVAL_UNSUPPORTED`, not
silently ignored, because a credential written into a query gets committed.
Never put a credential into a query to make it run; ask for the variable to be
set.
